tagline: Link client project tasks in Asana to Salesforce opportunities and accounts
metaTitle: Asana + Salesforce Integration: Closed Deals to Projects
metaDescription: Start delivery the moment a deal closes. GAIA creates an Asana project from each closed Salesforce deal and flags risks. See the setup steps.
intro:
Sales teams close deals in Salesforce while delivery teams execute projects in Asana, but the two rarely communicate. Account managers lack visibility into project delivery status without asking the delivery team directly. Delivery teams lack the account context that lives in the CRM. The result is a gap between what was sold and what is being delivered, with both teams working from incomplete information.

GAIA bridges the two so project delivery and client relationship management work together. When an opportunity closes, GAIA automatically creates a project with the right structure and assigns the delivery team. As project milestones are reached, GAIA updates the account record so account managers always know where delivery stands without interrupting the project team.

This integration is critical for professional services firms, SaaS companies with implementation teams, and agencies that need tight alignment between sales commitments and project delivery.

useCases.title: Create Asana projects from closed Salesforce opportunities
useCases.description: When an opportunity reaches Closed Won, GAIA automatically creates a corresponding project, assigns the delivery team, and populates tasks based on the contracted scope of work.

useCases.title: Sync project milestones to account records
useCases.description: When milestones are completed, GAIA updates the associated account with delivery status notes, giving account managers real-time project health visibility inside their CRM.

useCases.title: Escalate at-risk projects to account owners
useCases.description: When a project is flagged as at-risk or significantly overdue, GAIA creates a CRM task for the account owner to initiate a client conversation before the relationship is affected.

useCases.title: Log delivery milestones as Salesforce activities
useCases.description: Key project events, phase completions, go-live milestones, issue resolutions, are automatically logged as activity records, building a complete client history without manual data entry.

useCases.title: Upsell triggers from project completion
useCases.description: When a project is marked complete, GAIA creates a follow-up task for the account manager to explore renewal or upsell opportunities while the client relationship is at its strongest.

howItWorks.step: Connect Asana and Salesforce to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA to access your workspace and organization. Map opportunity fields to project fields so data transfers accurately between the two tools.
Define which opportunity stages trigger project creation, which milestone events update CRM records, and how accounts are linked to projects.

howItWorks.step: GAIA keeps delivery and CRM in sync
howItWorks.description: GAIA monitors both tools and propagates relevant events bidirectionally, ensuring sales and delivery teams always share an accurate, up-to-date view of each client engagement.

faqs.question: Can GAIA create different Asana project templates based on Salesforce opportunity type?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can configure GAIA to select project templates based on opportunity fields such as product line, contract value, or opportunity type, ensuring each project starts with the right task structure.

faqs.question: How does GAIA handle accounts with multiple active projects?
faqs.answer: GAIA links each project to the specific opportunity that generated it. Account-level summaries aggregate all linked projects so account managers see a complete delivery picture.

faqs.question: Can GAIA sync project budgets to opportunity values?
faqs.answer: GAIA can read contract value from the CRM and populate a custom project field for budget tracking. Actual-versus-planned budget analysis requires connecting your financial data source as well.
